headline: Buyers are flat owners already using self serve lease extension calculators online
whoPays: Flat owners who already use self serve lease extension calculators online, reached on that same estimate path.
proofPoint: GOV.UK lists 10,562 residential property tribunal decisions from December 2018 onwards for England (gov.uk residential property tribunal decisions).

title: Inheritance tax valuation reports for retirees
oneLine: A report, built on real HMRC settlement data, that shows a retiree or their family how to negotiate the valuation behind an inheritance tax bill.
cardLine: Report built on real HMRC settlement data
headline: HMRC settles valuation disputes at figures nobody outside the process gets to see
whoPays: A retiree aged 60 to 75 planning how to pass on a property or business, or the adult child helping settle an estate, reached through estate-planning solicitors and retirement newsletters.
proofPoint: Over 150,000 households could face new or higher inheritance tax bills after rule changes announced in the Labour Budget of October (Birmingham Mail).

title: Fixed cash payouts for tradespeople whose van fails MOT
oneLine: A one-person cover that pays a fixed cash sum to a self-employed tradesperson when their work van fails its MOT, so they can hire a replacement and keep working. The MOT result is public, so the payout runs off it automatically.
cardLine: Fixed payout to hire a van, no assessor visit
headline: Self employed tradespeople lose work when a van fails its MOT and must hire a replacement
whoPays: Self employed UK tradespeople reached through trade marketplaces like Checkatrade, where Superscript already sells insurance in five minutes or less.
proofPoint: Simply Business research reports tool theft cost tradespeople an estimated £98.9 million in the period covered, with average stolen tool claims up 24% since 2020.

title: Prefilled chemical safety assessments for nail technicians
oneLine: A downloadable set of pre-filled Control of Substances Hazardous to Health assessments for the common chemicals in nail services, so a mobile nail tech can show the inspector and get on with her day.
cardLine: Downloadable assessments for common nail service chemicals
headline: Nail techs face inspectors on chemical safety rules with no paperwork ready to show
whoPays: Self-employed nail technicians and mobile beauty therapists in the UK, reached through nail tech Facebook groups and open marketplaces such as Etsy.
proofPoint: Compliantdocs.co.uk advertises a filled nail technician compliance pack at £47.99, delivered in minutes.

title: Rating appeal service for UK delivery and rides drivers
oneLine: A dashboard that spots when a delivery or rides driver's rating drops, supplies the evidence templates, and files the appeal to get the score restored.
cardLine: Evidence templates and filed appeals, one rating at a time
headline: Ratings drop across delivery and rides apps and drivers have no easy way to challenge them
whoPays: UK delivery and rides drivers, reached through rider resource directories, Facebook rider groups, the Telegram tools riders already use, and union channels including the GMB Bolt noticeboard and IWGB social, email and WhatsApp groups.
proofPoint: MoneyMiles reports 2,300+ UK gig drivers paying £7.99 a month for its driver tool, showing workers in this group already buy software that protects their earnings.

title: Disability Living Allowance claim packs for parent carers
oneLine: A web app that turns a parent's daily-life notes into a DWP-ready Disability Living Allowance claim pack for a disabled child.
cardLine: Notes in, DWP-ready claim pack out
headline: A web app that turns a parent's daily-life notes into a claim pack ready for the DWP
whoPays: Parents caring for a disabled child, reached through parent carer Facebook groups and, on Mumsnet, through paid advertising rather than posts.
proofPoint: The DWP reports it cleared around 185,900 new child Disability Living Allowance claims between 1 August 2025 and 31 March 2026, with 68.3% (126,900) cleared within 45 working days (gov.uk).

title: UV lamp test cards for self-employed gel nail techs
oneLine: A colour-change card gel nail technicians use to test their UV/LED lamp, preventing undercured nails and allergic reactions.
cardLine: Colour-change cards plus a paper lamp-test log
headline: Gel nails cured under a weak lamp stay undercured, and undercured gel can trigger allergic reactions
whoPays: Self-employed UK gel nail technicians and mobile beauty therapists, reached through Facebook and Instagram.
proofPoint: The British Association of Dermatologists reports that 2.4% of people tested in a UK and Ireland study had an allergy to at least one methacrylate chemical found in gel and acrylic nails.

title: Booking calendar and owner updates for solo pet sitters
oneLine: A web app that pulls pet-sitting bookings from Rover, Cat in a Flat and direct messages into one calendar, auto-sends photos to owners, and chases reviews, for the gig worker juggling multiple pet-care apps.
cardLine: One calendar, auto photo updates, review chasing
headline: Sitters juggle Rover, Cat in a Flat and direct messages, with no single calendar across them
whoPays: Solo UK pet sitters on gig platforms, who already gather in UK Rover Facebook groups and the r/RoverPetSitting forum.
proofPoint: UK dog walker pay is reported at £26,436 to £39,860 a year, with hourly rates of £12.71 to £19 (Salary Expert; Glassdoor).

title: Street trading licence tracker for market traders
oneLine: A web app that tracks a trader's street trading licences across every UK council, fills in each council's paperwork, and warns them before a pitch lapses.
cardLine: Auto fills the paperwork, warns before a pitch lapses
headline: Traders holding pitches in more than one UK council area risk losing them to missed renewals
whoPays: Mobile food vendors, market stallholders and street entertainers who hold street trading licences in more than one UK council area, reached through the National Market Traders Federation and similar trade channels.
proofPoint: The National Market Traders Federation, described as the UK's only national body for market and street traders, events retailers and mobile caterers, reports around 22,000 members (source: memberwise.org.uk).

title: Notifiable-work certification for sole-trader electricians
oneLine: A fixed-fee service that certifies notifiable domestic electrical work without the electrician needing building control or a competent-person scheme.
cardLine: Inspect and certify other electricians' domestic wiring
headline: A worked plan for setting up to certify other electricians' domestic wiring
whoPays: Self employed electricians in England who do work that has to be notified to building control. UK electrician forums and public electrician groups are where they gather, though no source here shows those venues welcome selling.
proofPoint: An electrical training site's article reports self employed electricians mentioning day rates of £250 to £350 and annual earnings north of £60,000. That is one site's summary of what electricians say, not a survey.

title: Frost-day income cover for self-employed bricklayers
oneLine: A parametric bond that pays a fixed daily sum to a bricklayer for each day the Met Office records a ground frost at their postcode during the laying season.
cardLine: Pays a fixed sum per postcode frost day
headline: A worked plan for selling frost day income cover to self employed bricklayers
whoPays: Self employed bricklayers who work outdoors through the winter, approached through online bricklayer communities and builders' merchant trade counters, neither of which is an agreed route yet.
proofPoint: One bricklaying company's own winter guidance (slbcltd.co.uk) states that when the temperature is 3°C and falling, bricklayers cannot and should not build, because of the impact frost has on build quality. That is a single firm's public advice, not a measured count of lost days across the trade.

title: Harvest, purge or hold calls for UK shellfish farms
oneLine: Tells an oyster or mussel farm whether to harvest, purge or hold each lease, by combining live sewage discharge data, rainfall, tides and past water testing results. The farmer acts before a closure instead of losing the crop to it.
cardLine: Tells a farm to harvest, purge or hold, lease by lease
headline: Owner run oyster and mussel farms judge each lease from storm overflow, rain and tide data
whoPays: Owner operated UK shellfish farms, reached through the Shellfish Association of Great Britain newsletter, SAGB Conference and Dinner, and Local Action Groups.
proofPoint: Cefas states purification requires a minimum of 42 hours in seawater tanks, and only stock from class B areas (and where deemed necessary class A) may be depurated (Cefas depuration advice).

title: Daily income cover for stone worktop fabricators
oneLine: Pays a self-employed worktop fabricator a fixed sum for every day their workshop is closed by a Health and Safety Executive notice over stone dust. The price is set from dust readings the operator collects workshop by workshop.
cardLine: A fixed daily sum while the workshop is shut down
headline: Roughly 2,000 to 3,000 UK workshops run by owners who cannot survive four weeks of zero fabrication
whoPays: Self-employed and 1-3 person stone/quartz worktop fabrication and masonry workshops in the UK (roughly 2,000-3,000 units, concentrated around Leeds, Birmingham, Essex and Glasgow trade parks), the owner-fabricator himself, who has business budget authority, already buys £2k+/yr of tooling and PPE, and cannot survive four weeks of zero fabrication.
proofPoint: value durability: The passages show active, coordinated regulatory enforcement against respirable crystalline silica in stone/concrete work by UK-jurisdiction and Irish regulators

title: Back payment claims for unpaid carers on Universal Credit
oneLine: Rebuilds a carer's Universal Credit history, finds the months the Carer Element was never awarded, and files the backdated claims across Universal Credit, Council Tax Reduction and the linked disability schemes in one run. Paid only on money actually recovered.
cardLine: Rebuild claim history, file missed months for a share
headline: Primary carers on Universal Credit can have un-awarded Carer Element months going unclaimed
whoPays: Primary carers already on Universal Credit who suspect missed carer element months, reached through NHS hospital discharge teams and local carer centres.
proofPoint: Carers UK's State of Caring 2025, cited in a 20 November 2025 Westminster Hall debate, records 1.2 million unpaid carers across the UK in poverty, 400,000 in deep poverty, and four in ten not knowing what benefits they are entitled to.

title: Prepaid fee recovery service for parents of closed nurseries
oneLine: When a nursery closes mid term, this recovers the parent's prepaid fees and deposit from the administrator, card issuer, funding authority and childcare voucher scheme at the same time, then moves the child into a new place within the week. Paid per channel recovered.
cardLine: Fixed fee per recovery, one closed setting at a time
headline: When a nursery or childminding agency folds mid-term, parents lose prepaid fees and deposits
whoPays: Parent-carers of children at a specific closed nursery or childminding agency, reached through the parent group that forms around the closure and through public listings of affected settings
proofPoint: Daily Mail documents a £200 non-refundable deposit plus admin fee at Kids Unlimited, the kind of prepaid money stranded when a nursery closes

title: DWP underpayment audits for adult children of retirees
oneLine: A dataset of tribunal outcomes and DWP recalculation rules, built from freedom of information requests. It sells as a £149 audit of one retired parent to their adult children, and as a £1,200 a year bulk licence to solicitors and independent financial advisers.
cardLine: £149 an audit, built from tribunal outcome data
headline: Adult children pay £149 an audit, and solicitors pay £1,200 a year for the bulk licence
whoPays: Adult children of retired parents pay £149 per audit. Private client solicitors and IFAs, reachable through the STEP directory, pay £1,200 a year for the bulk licence.
proofPoint: DWP's own review process found 119,050 underpayments worth £736 million between January 2021 and September 2024 (gov.uk).
